sounds.name: First Sounds
sounds.ref: The guide’s Getting Started: CLOCK set, PLAY/STOP pressed, the sequencer running
sounds.blurb: The guide’s first steps: set the clock, press PLAY/STOP, and the EDGE plays a pattern.
sounds.how: The guide starts with the volume up, CLOCK set, the controls as its default patch drawing and PLAY/STOP pressed. The drawing’s knob positions are not transcribed, so this is the plainest pattern from the Default patch: a short, round hit with a little punch on an accented row. CLOCK is on MIDI here, so the app’s clock runs it at SCALE 1/16; the guide uses INT.

steps.title: A little punch
steps.why:
OSC 1 at A1 with its ENVELOPE turned right: each hit starts with a pitch spike.
- OSC 1 FREQUENCY 3.75 · A1 · 55 Hz
- OSC 1 EG AMOUNT 2.5 · +24 st at full velocity
- EG (OSC 1&2) DECAY 2.33 · 50 ms
- Listen for: with a key, a short, round, punchy hit.

sounds.name: Cross-Mod Toms
sounds.ref: The guide’s first patch idea: OSC 1 into OSC 2 CV
sounds.blurb: Gnarly, growling toms: OSC 1 modulating OSC 2’s pitch through a cable.
sounds.how: OSC 1 patched into OSC 2 CV is exponential FM, the guide’s first idea: unlike the 1-2 FM AMT knob’s linear FM it bends OSC 2’s pitch unevenly, rough and growling. OSC 2 is the only one in the mix. The guide names the cable and no knob positions, so the settings around it are this lesson’s.

steps.title: OSC 2 alone, a tom
steps.why:
OSC 1 out of the mix at D2; OSC 2 triangle at A2 in the mix, with a pitch drop.
- OSC 1 LEVEL 0
- OSC 2 LEVEL 8
- OSC 1 FREQUENCY 4.17 · D2 · 74 Hz
- OSC 2 FREQUENCY 4.75 · A2 · 110 Hz
- OSC 2 EG AMOUNT 1.77 · +12 st at full velocity
- EG (OSC 1&2) DECAY 3.33 · 100 ms
- DECAY (VCA) 4.92 · 300 ms
- Listen for: with a key, a plain falling tom.

sounds.name: Hats by PITCH
sounds.ref: The guide’s second patch idea: PITCH into VCA DECAY
sounds.blurb: Pink-noise hats, each step’s length set by its PITCH knob.
sounds.how: PITCH into VCA DECAY makes the PITCH row a row of lengths: turned up for an open hat, centred for a closed one. Pink noise gives a softer, darker hat than the DFAM’s white. The guide names the cable and no knob positions, so the settings around it are this lesson’s.

steps.why:
OSC 1 down, NOISE/EXT up, COLOR on PINK, the filter on HP at 5 kHz.
- OSC 1 LEVEL 0
- NOISE / EXT LEVEL 10
- NOISE COLOR Pink
- VCF SELECT HP
- CUTOFF 7.99 · 5.0 kHz
- DECAY (VCA) 2.01 · 40 ms
- Listen for: with a key, a soft, dark tick.

sounds.name: Velocity FM Bells
sounds.ref: The guide’s third patch idea: VELOCITY into 1-2 FM AMT
sounds.blurb: A bell pattern whose accents clang: the VEL row also sets the FM.
sounds.how: VELOCITY into 1-2 FM AMT adds each step’s velocity to the FM depth, so the VEL row sets brightness as well as loudness. The guide names the cable and no knob positions, so the settings around it are this lesson’s.

sounds.name: Triplet Hats
sounds.ref: Hi-hats in eighth-note triplets against a straight beat
sounds.how: SCALE divides the MIDI clock into triplets as well as straight notes. On 1/8T, three steps a beat: the eight steps then cross the bar line and line up again every two bars, rolling against the drums.

sounds.name: Pink Snare
sounds.ref: A fat, dark snare of tone and pink noise
sounds.blurb: A darker, fatter snare than white noise gives.
sounds.how: A snare is a tone for the head and noise for the wires. Pink noise keeps more of its energy low, so the wires sound fatter and darker.

sounds.name: Club Kick
sounds.ref: A punchy four-on-the-floor kick locked to MIDI clock
sounds.blurb: A tight kick on every beat, from MIDI clock at 1/4.
sounds.how: At SCALE 1/4 each step is a beat, so every step with velocity is a kick on the beat: with all eight steps up, a kick on every beat for two bars. A low triangle with a fast pitch drop.

sounds.name: MIDI Bass
sounds.ref: A plucky analogue bass played from MIDI notes
sounds.blurb: The EDGE played as a bass synth: MIDI notes, here the keys, with the sequencer stopped.
sounds.how: MIDI notes play the EDGE’s voice: the note’s pitch moves both oscillators, and its velocity strikes the envelopes. With the sequencer stopped, it is a monosynth with three decay envelopes. A square and a triangle in unison, a resonant filter plucked by its envelope.

steps.title: Two oscillators in unison
steps.why:
OSC 1 square and OSC 2 triangle at C2, a key’s C3 an octave up.
- OSC 1 FREQUENCY 4 · C2 · 65 Hz
- OSC 1 SHAPE Square
- OSC 2 FREQUENCY 4 · C2 · 65 Hz
- OSC 2 LEVEL 6
- Listen for: with a key, a full, low tone.

steps.title: Pluck
steps.why:
CUTOFF at 400 Hz, RESONANCE at 4, the filter envelope two and a half octaves, a 300 ms decay.
- CUTOFF 4.34 · 401 Hz
- RESONANCE 4
- ENVELOPE (FILTER) 1.56 · +2.5 oct at full velocity
- DECAY (FILTER) 3.92 · 150 ms
- DECAY (VCA) 4.92 · 300 ms
- Listen for: play a bass line: plucky, round notes, brighter the harder you press.

sounds.name: Played Percussion
sounds.ref: A conga-like hand drum played from MIDI notes
sounds.blurb: A hand drum on the keys: each key a pitch, each hit as hard as you play it.
sounds.how: From MIDI notes the EDGE is a drum module: the note sets the pitch, the velocity the strength of the hit. A triangle with a small pitch drop and a resonant filter makes a conga.

sounds.name: Free-Running Clock
sounds.ref: The internal clock run up to buzzing rolls
sounds.blurb: CLOCK on INT/EXT and TEMPO high: the steps run past the beat into a buzzing roll.
sounds.how: On INT/EXT the TEMPO knob runs the clock, an oscillator from 0.7 to 700 Hz. Here it is locked to the bar while it is slow enough to be a tempo, but turned up past about twenty steps a second it runs free: the eight steps blur into a buzzing, pitched roll whose pitch is the clock’s rate.
